segments.he: כל הפגמים שבעולם הוא בחי׳ פגם בכבוד ה/ כי כל התורה היא בשביל כבודו ית׳, וכשפוגמין באיזה חטא שבעולם ח״ו ובפרט פגם הברית שהוא עיקר הכל, עי״ז פוגמין בכבודו ית׳, ואז נתרחק הנפש מן הכבוד, וכפי הפגם כן הריחוק, וכן נופל הכבוד ח״ו אל העכו״ם והרשעים. ויש בזה כמה בחי׳ בלי שיעור בענין פגם נפילת הכבוד ובענין התרחקות הנפש מן הכבוד. וע״כ במקום קברי הצדיק?,ם ששם מקום אסיפתן ושם שורה כבוד ה׳ בחי׳ כבוד ה׳ יאספך הנאמר על הסתלקות וקבורת הצדיק כמובן בדברי רז״ל. ע״כ שם עיקר התיקון לכל הפגמים בפרט לפגם הברית, וע״י שחוזרת הנפש אל הכבוד עי״ז זוכין להתפלל בכוונה ובלב שלם, וזה בחי׳ מה שמתעוררין מאד על קברי צדיקים אמתיים ומתפללין ומתחננין שם בהתעוררות הלב מאד ושופכים שם לבם כמים לפני ה׳. וזה מחמת ששם מתקרבת הנפש אל הכבוד ביותר שמשם נמשך תפלה
segments.en: But even so: "and You, Hashem, are exalted forever" — for the Tzaddikim strive and toil in this matter so greatly for the benefit of Yisrael, and do not depart from the world until they merit, on the day of their passing, to sanctify the air of the world with such wondrous holiness — that no dispute and no stormy wind will have power to confuse the air. Rather their words will go forth and spread through the world and be heard from afar, in the aspect of: "your springs will spread outward" [Mishlei 5:16] — until the whole world returns and comes back through this to Hashem.

segments.he: השתטחות בכוונה ובלב שלם במבואר בפנים (חובל בחבירו ה״ג אות יו״ד).
segments.en: And even though the stormy wind seems great in its time — and it has been already more than a hundred years since the passing of the Baal Shem Tov of blessed memory, and yet there are still many who dispute against him — and all the more so against his followers and holy disciples. And so it is in every generation. Even so, in the end the truth will be revealed — and "a truthful lip is established forever" [Mishlei 12:19]. And even now, with Hashem's help, there are already many who recognize the truth and cherish the words of the Tzaddikim without measure and see and understand a little of the great wonders of the holiness of their Torah and their holy and supremely elevated attainment. For the Tzaddikim are greater in their death than in their lifetimes. And specifically through the passing — when their holy soul, spirit, and neshamah depart to return to their source — and a great illumination remains from the remnant of their soul in this world at their holy grave, as explained in the writings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory — through this the entire air of the world is sanctified with great holiness, so that their holy words will always be heard from afar. And this is the virtue of the holiness of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for there the air is very holy, the purest and most pleasant air. And through this one merits to hear the voice of the words of the true Tzaddik — all of whose words throughout his life were to draw holy faith into the world. And through this the good that is suppressed within each person is aroused and returns to its elevation. And therefore it is good to learn at the graves of the Tzaddikim from their Torah innovations — for there, since the air is pure and pleasant, a person can merit that the words of the true Tzaddikim are properly heard within his heart — until he returns to Hashem. And therefore charity is given abundantly at the graves of the Tzaddikim — for charity is propitious for drawing pure and pleasant air — and through this one merits even more to be included in the holy pure and pleasant air that is at the graves of the true Tzaddikim.
